description: openLCA 2.8.2 names metal ions with a Stock numeral or the generic marker -- `Cadmium II`, `Arsenic V`, `Copper Ion` -- and writes the bare metal's registry number on 339 of those rows under 29 names: 7440-43-9 on `Cadmium II`, 7439-92-1 on `Lead II`. The number route runs before the name route, so on the six-list build of 21 October 2026 (commit 931ed30) every one of them reached the metal, while the sibling rows carrying the ion's own number reached the ion: `Cadmium II` was two substances depending on which number came with it, and the lookup read the name three ways (#380). The merge now sets a bare element's number aside where the row's name states an ion (`merge.species.element_number_set_aside`), the row is placed by its name through the ion naming standard, and the mapping's basis reads `label+element-number-set-aside` with the number. The lookup prepares a query the same way. One claim per name; the two substance claims hold the numbers apart.

expectations.comment: On the six-list build of 21 October 2026 (commit 931ed30) the 10 rows reached `Aluminium` by the number. The number is the metal's; the name says the ion.

expectations.title: One substance carries cadmium's number 7440-43-9 and it is called Cadmium
expectations.comment: The rule sets the number aside rather than carrying it onto the ion: a `Cadmium(2+)` under the metal's number would be a second substance on the number, which the number route would then find for every bare `Cadmium` row.
